beats.narration_text: Hi — I'm Sudhanva, and this is a project update for the RL Environments project. The project: train a colony of ant agents to forage, first alone, then together. The update: I've started the research; the implementation comes next. Here's what I found.

props.runningText: reading the multi-agent RL and ant-transport literature…
output: Independent learners hold up until coordination matters (Papoudakis et al., 2021)
Loosen with shared training, separate action: VDN · QMIX · MAPPO

beats.act: Act 1 — FRAMEWORK: two worlds, four jobs, the ant spec
beats.narration_text: Two worlds: a grid, and open continuous space. Four jobs: find food, bring it home, cut big food into pieces, and carry the pieces together — the way real ants do, feeling each other's pull through the load.

beats.narration_text: Stage one: every ant learns alone — independent Q-learning, its own reward. Benchmarks say that works until a task needs coordination. Stage two loosens the policies: train together, act alone. VDN adds the ants' values into one team score; QMIX mixes them so an ant's gain never lowers the team's.

beats.narration_text: Where it breaks: sparse rewards. On one warehouse benchmark, value decomposition learned nothing. And with a shared reward, one ant can coast while the others haul — so I'll measure every ant's share.
